questions.q: What is a noun?
options: A naming word — a person, place, or thing
questions.answer: A naming word — a person, place, or thing
questions.explain: A noun names a person, place, thing, or idea.
procedure: A noun is a naming word
Answer: A naming word — a person, place, or thing

questions.q: Which of these is a noun?
questions.explain: 'Teacher' is a noun — it names a person.
procedure: Nouns name people, places, or things

questions.q: What is a verb?
options: An action word or state of being
questions.answer: An action word or state of being
questions.explain: A verb shows action or state of being.
procedure: They show what someone or something does
Verbs also show states of being (is, are, was)
Answer: An action word or state of being

questions.q: Which of these is a verb?
questions.explain: 'Dance' is a verb — it shows an action.

questions.q: What is an adjective?
options: A word that describes a noun
A word that describes a verb
questions.answer: A word that describes a noun
questions.explain: Adjectives describe or add meaning to nouns.
procedure: They tell us what kind, how many, or which one
Answer: A word that describes a noun

questions.q: Which word is an adjective in this sentence: 'The tall boy ran quickly.'
questions.explain: 'Tall' describes the noun 'boy' — so it's an adjective.
procedure: What kind of boy? A 'tall' boy

questions.q: What is an adverb?
options: A word that describes a noun
A word that describes a verb, adjective, or another adverb
questions.answer: A word that describes a verb, adjective, or another adverb
questions.explain: Adverbs describe how, when, or where an action happens.
procedure: Adverbs describe verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs
They can answer: how? when? where?
Answer: A word that describes a verb, adjective, or another adverb

questions.q: Which word is an adverb in this sentence: 'She sang beautifully.'
questions.explain: 'Beautifully' describes how she sang — so it's an adverb.
procedure: Adverbs tell us HOW something happened

questions.q: What is a pronoun?
options: A word that replaces a noun
questions.answer: A word that replaces a noun
questions.explain: Pronouns replace nouns — like he, she, it, they, we.
procedure: A pronoun stands in place of a noun
Instead of saying 'Kofi ran', we say 'He ran'
Examples: I, you, he, she, it, we, they
Answer: A word that replaces a noun

questions.q: Which of these is a pronoun?
questions.explain: 'She' is a pronoun — it replaces a female person's name.

questions.q: What is a preposition?
options: A word that shows the position or relationship between things
questions.answer: A word that shows the position or relationship between things
questions.explain: Prepositions show relationships — in, on, under, beside, between.
procedure: Examples: in, on, under, beside, between
The cat is UNDER the table
Answer: A word that shows the position or relationship between things

questions.q: Which of these is a preposition?
questions.explain: 'Under' is a preposition — it shows position.

questions.q: What is a conjunction?
questions.explain: Conjunctions join words, phrases, or sentences — and, but, or, because.
procedure: Examples: and, but, or, because, so

questions.q: Which of these is a conjunction?
questions.explain: 'And' joins two ideas together — it's a conjunction.

questions.q: Which word is a noun in the sentence: 'The red car is fast.'
questions.explain: 'Car' is a noun — it names a thing.

questions.q: What is the noun in: 'They live in Kumasi.'
questions.explain: 'Kumasi' is a noun — it names a place.
procedure: Nouns name people, places, or things

questions.q: Which of these sentences uses an adjective?
questions.explain: 'Big' describes 'dog' — so it's an adjective.
procedure: Answer: The big dog barks loudly.

questions.q: Identify the verb in: 'The children play football.'
questions.explain: 'Play' is a verb — it's the action the children do.
procedure: What are the children doing? Playing

questions.q: Identify the adverb in: 'They arrived late.'
questions.explain: 'Late' describes when they arrived — so it's an adverb.
procedure: Adverbs tell us WHEN, HOW, or WHERE

questions.q: Which part of speech is the word 'quickly'?
questions.explain: 'Quickly' tells us HOW something is done — it's an adverb.
procedure: It describes how something is done

questions.q: Which part of speech is the word 'happy'?
questions.explain: 'Happy' is an adjective — it describes a noun (a happy person).
procedure: A 'happy' person = happy describes the person

questions.q: What is the present tense?
options: It shows actions in the past
It shows actions in the future
It shows actions that never happen
questions.explain: The present tense describes actions happening now.
procedure: The action is happening in the present
Answer: It shows actions happening now

questions.q: What is the past tense?
options: It shows actions that already happened
questions.answer: It shows actions that already happened
questions.explain: The past tense describes actions that already happened.
procedure: Answer: It shows actions that already happened

questions.q: What is the future tense?
options: It shows actions that have not yet happened
questions.answer: It shows actions that have not yet happened
questions.explain: The future tense describes actions that will happen.
procedure: Answer: It shows actions that have not yet happened

questions.q: Choose the correct past tense: 'Yesterday, I ____ to school.'
questions.explain: 'Went' is the past tense of 'go'.

questions.q: Choose the correct future tense: 'Tomorrow, she ____ her grandmother.'
questions.explain: 'Will visit' is the future tense — it shows what will happen tomorrow.

questions.q: Which sentence is in the present tense?
questions.explain: 'Walk' is present tense — the action happens now.
procedure: Present tense uses the base verb

questions.q: What is the present continuous tense?
options: It shows an action happening right now
It shows an action in the past
It shows an action in the future
It shows an action that never happened
questions.answer: It shows an action happening right now
questions.explain: Present continuous shows actions happening right now — I am walking.
procedure: The action is happening RIGHT NOW
Answer: It shows an action happening right now

questions.q: Choose the correct present continuous: 'Look! The baby ____.'
questions.explain: 'Is crying' is present continuous — the baby is crying right now.

questions.q: Which is the past tense of 'eat'?
questions.explain: 'Ate' is the correct past tense of 'eat'.

questions.q: Which is the past tense of 'run'?
questions.explain: 'Ran' is the correct past tense of 'run'.

questions.q: Which of these is a future tense sentence?
questions.explain: 'Will eat' shows a future action.

questions.q: Which is correct: 'She ____ her homework already.'
questions.explain: 'Already' suggests the action is complete — past tense.

questions.q: What is the correct present continuous of 'sleep' in: 'The cat ____ on the sofa.'
questions.explain: The cat is sleeping — present continuous, happening right now.

questions.q: Which is the past continuous tense?
questions.explain: Past continuous uses 'was/were + verb-ing'.
procedure: 'I was walking' = an action that was happening in the past

questions.q: Choose the correct form: 'By next year, I ____ in this school for three years.'
questions.explain: 'By next year' means the future — so 'will be' is correct.
procedure: 'By next year' is a future phrase

questions.q: Which sentence uses the present tense correctly?
options: She go to school every day.
She goes to school every day.
She going to school every day.
She gone to school every day.
questions.answer: She goes to school every day.
questions.explain: 'She' is singular, so the verb needs 's' — goes.
procedure: 'She goes to school every day' is correct
Answer: She goes to school every day.

questions.q: Which is the correct past tense: 'They ____ football yesterday.'
questions.explain: 'Yesterday' needs past tense — 'played'.

questions.q: What does 'has eaten' show?
options: Present perfect — action completed before now
questions.answer: Present perfect — action completed before now
questions.explain: 'Has eaten' is present perfect — an action finished at some point before now.
procedure: 'Has eaten' = finished eating at some point
Answer: Present perfect — action completed before now

questions.q: Which is correct: 'I ____ to Accra next week.'
questions.explain: 'Am going' can be used for planned future events.
procedure: For planned future, use 'am/is/are going to'
'I am going to Accra next week'

questions.q: Choose the correct past tense: 'The birds ____ away when I opened the door.'
questions.explain: 'Flew' is the past tense of 'fly'.
procedure: 'Opened' is past, so 'fly' should also be past

questions.q: What is a synonym?
options: A word with the opposite meaning
A word with the same or similar meaning
A word borrowed from another language
questions.answer: A word with the same or similar meaning
questions.explain: Synonyms are words with similar meanings.
procedure: Answer: A word with the same or similar meaning

questions.q: Which word is a synonym for 'happy'?
questions.explain: 'Glad' is a synonym for 'happy'.
procedure: Happy and glad both mean joyful

questions.q: Which word is a synonym for 'big'?
questions.explain: 'Huge' is a synonym for 'big'.
procedure: Big and huge both mean large

questions.q: What is an antonym?
options: A word with the same meaning
A word with the opposite meaning
questions.answer: A word with the opposite meaning
questions.explain: Antonyms are words with opposite meanings.
procedure: Answer: A word with the opposite meaning

questions.q: Which is an antonym for 'hot'?
questions.explain: 'Cold' is the antonym of 'hot'.
procedure: The opposite of hot is cold

questions.q: Which is an antonym for 'brave'?
questions.explain: 'Cowardly' is the antonym of 'brave'.
procedure: Its opposite is cowardly = lacking courage

questions.q: What are homophones?
options: Words that sound the same but are spelled differently
Words with the same spelling but different meanings
questions.answer: Words that sound the same but are spelled differently
questions.explain: Homophones sound the same but have different spellings and meanings.
procedure: Answer: Words that sound the same but are spelled differently

questions.q: Which pair are homophones?
questions.explain: 'There' and 'their' sound the same — they're homophones.

questions.q: Which word is a synonym for 'quick'?
questions.explain: 'Fast' is a synonym for 'quick'.
procedure: Quick and fast mean the same thing

questions.q: Which word is an antonym for 'strong'?
questions.explain: 'Weak' is the opposite of 'strong'.

questions.q: What is the meaning of 'ancient'?
questions.explain: 'Ancient' means very old — from a long time ago.
procedure: Example: ancient Egypt = Egypt from a very long time ago

questions.q: What is the meaning of 'enormous'?
questions.explain: 'Enormous' means very large or huge.
procedure: An enormous elephant = a huge elephant

questions.q: What does 'brave' mean?
options: Ready to face danger without fear
questions.answer: Ready to face danger without fear
questions.explain: 'Brave' means having courage to face danger.
procedure: Answer: Ready to face danger without fear

questions.q: What is the meaning of 'gather'?
questions.explain: 'Gather' means to bring things or people together.
procedure: She gathered stones = collected them together

questions.q: Which word means 'to look at something carefully'?
questions.explain: 'Examine' means to look at something carefully.
procedure: Doctors examine patients — look at them carefully

questions.q: What is the meaning of 'difficult'?
questions.explain: 'Difficult' means hard — not easy.
procedure: A difficult question = a hard question
Answer: Not easy — hard to do

questions.q: What is the meaning of 'furious'?
questions.explain: 'Furious' means extremely angry.
procedure: He was furious = he was very angry

questions.q: What does 'curious' mean?
options: Wanting to know or learn something
questions.answer: Wanting to know or learn something
questions.explain: 'Curious' means wanting to know or learn more.
procedure: A curious child asks many questions
Answer: Wanting to know or learn something

questions.q: Which word means 'to say sorry'?
questions.explain: 'Apologize' means to say sorry.
procedure: I apologize for being late = I am sorry for being late

questions.q: What is the meaning of 'immediately'?
questions.explain: 'Immediately' means right now, without delay.

questions.q: What does a full stop (.) show?
options: That a question is being asked
questions.explain: A full stop marks the end of a sentence.
procedure: A full stop is a small dot (.)
It marks the end of a statement
Answer: That a sentence has ended

questions.q: Which sentence needs a full stop?
questions.explain: All three need punctuation — 'What is your name?' (question mark), 'I love mangoes.' (full stop), 'Help!' (exclamation mark).
procedure: Every sentence needs an end punctuation
Statements end with a full stop
Questions end with a question mark
Exclamations end with an exclamation mark

questions.q: What does a question mark (?) show?
options: That a question is being asked
questions.answer: That a question is being asked
questions.explain: A question mark shows that a question is being asked.
procedure: It goes at the end of a question
Answer: That a question is being asked

questions.q: Which sentence needs a question mark?
questions.explain: 'Where are you going' is a question — it needs a question mark.
procedure: 'Where are you going?' is a question
So it needs a question mark

questions.q: What does an exclamation mark (!) show?
options: That a sentence is a statement
That a sentence is a question
Strong emotion — surprise, excitement, or a command
questions.answer: Strong emotion — surprise, excitement, or a command
questions.explain: An exclamation mark shows strong emotion or a command.
procedure: Answer: Strong emotion — surprise, excitement, or a command

questions.q: Which sentence needs an exclamation mark?
questions.explain: 'Wow that is amazing' shows surprise — it needs an exclamation mark.

questions.q: What does a comma (,) do?
options: Shows the end of a sentence
Separates items in a list or pauses a sentence
questions.answer: Separates items in a list or pauses a sentence
questions.explain: A comma separates items in a list or creates a small pause.
procedure: Example: 'I bought apples, oranges, and bananas.'
It also creates pauses in longer sentences
Answer: Separates items in a list or pauses a sentence

questions.q: Which sentence uses commas correctly?
options: I like red blue and green.
I like red, blue, and green.
I like red, blue and, green.
questions.answer: I like red, blue, and green.
questions.explain: Commas separate list items — 'red, blue, and green'.
procedure: The comma before 'and' is optional but common
Answer: I like red, blue, and green.

questions.q: What does an apostrophe (') show?
options: That something is missing or belongs to someone
That someone is asking a question
questions.answer: That something is missing or belongs to someone
questions.explain: Apostrophes show possession or missing letters.
procedure: 1. Possession: 'Kofi's book' (the book belongs to Kofi)
Answer: That something is missing or belongs to someone

questions.q: Which is correct?
questions.explain: 'Kofi's book' shows the book belongs to Kofi — using an apostrophe.
procedure: For possession, add 's after the noun
'Kofi's book' = the book belongs to Kofi

questions.q: What does 'don't' stand for?
questions.explain: 'Don't' is a contraction — the apostrophe replaces the missing 'o' in 'not'.
procedure: The apostrophe stands for the missing 'o'

questions.q: Which sentence has correct punctuation?
questions.explain: 'What is your name' is a question — it needs a question mark.
procedure: 'What is your name?' is a question
So it needs a question mark

questions.q: Where does a comma belong in this sentence: 'I bought bread milk and eggs.'
questions.explain: Commas separate list items: 'bread, milk, and eggs.'
procedure: Correct: 'I bought bread, milk, and eggs.'
Commas go after each item except the last

questions.q: What is the correct contraction of 'it is'?
questions.explain: 'It's' with an apostrophe is the contraction of 'it is'.
procedure: The apostrophe replaces the missing 'i' in 'is'
Note: 'its' (no apostrophe) is a different word — it shows possession

questions.q: Which sentence uses an apostrophe correctly?
questions.explain: 'Dog's' shows the tail belongs to the dog — correct apostrophe usage.
procedure: 'Dog's tail' = the tail of the dog

questions.q: What does a colon (:) do?
options: Shows a pause before a list or explanation
questions.answer: Shows a pause before a list or explanation
questions.explain: A colon introduces a list, explanation, or quotation.
procedure: It introduces a list or explanation
Example: 'I need three things: bread, milk, and eggs.'
Answer: Shows a pause before a list or explanation

questions.q: What does a semicolon (;) do?
questions.explain: A semicolon joins two related complete sentences.
procedure: It joins two complete sentences that are related
Example: 'I like tea; my brother likes coffee.'
Answer: Joins two closely related sentences

questions.q: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
questions.explain: Capitalise the first word and names of people.
procedure: Capitalise names of people, places, days

questions.q: Which of these should be capitalised?
questions.explain: Days of the week are always capitalised: Monday.
procedure: Days, months, and places need capital first letters

questions.q: What does a hyphen (-) do?
questions.explain: A hyphen joins words — like 'well-known' or 'twenty-one'.
procedure: It joins words that work together

questions.q:
Passage: 'Kofi woke up early on Monday. He ate his breakfast quickly because he did not want to be late for school. He wore his blue uniform and walked to school with his sister.'

Why did Kofi eat breakfast quickly?
options: He did not want to be late for school
He did not like the food
questions.answer: He did not want to be late for school
questions.explain: The passage says 'because he did not want to be late for school.'
procedure: Find the sentence that explains WHY
The passage says: 'He ate his breakfast quickly because he did not want to be late for school.'
Answer: He did not want to be late for school

questions.q:
Passage: 'Kofi woke up early on Monday. He ate his breakfast quickly because he did not want to be late for school. He wore his blue uniform and walked to school with his sister.'

What colour was Kofi's uniform?
questions.explain: The passage says 'he wore his blue uniform'.
procedure: Scan the passage for the word 'uniform'

questions.q:
Passage: 'Kofi woke up early on Monday. He ate his breakfast quickly because he did not want to be late for school. He wore his blue uniform and walked to school with his sister.'

Who did Kofi walk to school with?
questions.explain: The passage says 'walked to school with his sister'.
procedure: Find the part about walking to school
'He walked to school with his sister'

questions.q:
Passage: 'Ama loves animals. She has a dog named Rex and two cats. Every morning, she feeds them before school. She wants to be a vet when she grows up.'

Why does Ama want to be a vet?
questions.explain: The passage says 'Ama loves animals' — that's why she wants to be a vet.
procedure: Look for the reason she wants to be a vet
The first line says: 'Ama loves animals'
A vet helps animals — she wants to be one because she loves them

questions.q:
Passage: 'Ama loves animals. She has a dog named Rex and two cats. Every morning, she feeds them before school. She wants to be a vet when she grows up.'

How many pets does Ama have?
questions.explain: She has one dog (Rex) + two cats = three pets.

questions.q:
Passage: 'The rain fell heavily for three days. The river near the village began to rise. The villagers worried that it might flood their homes.'

Why were the villagers worried?
options: They thought their homes might be flooded
questions.answer: They thought their homes might be flooded
questions.explain: The passage says they worried the river might flood their homes.
procedure: The last sentence explains the worry
'The villagers worried that it might flood their homes'
Answer: They thought their homes might be flooded

questions.q:
Passage: 'The rain fell heavily for three days. The river near the village began to rise. The villagers worried that it might flood their homes.'

How long did the rain fall?
questions.explain: The passage says 'the rain fell heavily for three days'.
procedure: Find how long the rain lasted
'The rain fell heavily for three days'

questions.q:
Passage: 'Akosua is a hardworking student. She wakes up at 5 AM every day to study. Her teachers say she is the best student in her class.'

What time does Akosua wake up?
questions.explain: The passage says 'she wakes up at 5 AM every day'.
procedure: 'She wakes up at 5 AM every day'

questions.q:
Passage: 'Akosua is a hardworking student. She wakes up at 5 AM every day to study. Her teachers say she is the best student in her class.'

What do her teachers say about her?
options: She is the best student in her class
questions.answer: She is the best student in her class
questions.explain: The passage says 'her teachers say she is the best student in her class'.
procedure: 'Her teachers say she is the best student in her class'
Answer: She is the best student in her class

questions.q:
Passage: 'It was market day in Kumasi. The market was full of people. Traders were selling yams, plantains, tomatoes, and fish. Everyone was busy and happy.'

Where did this story take place?
questions.explain: The passage says 'It was market day in Kumasi'.

questions.q:
Passage: 'It was market day in Kumasi. The market was full of people. Traders were selling yams, plantains, tomatoes, and fish. Everyone was busy and happy.'

What were the traders selling?
questions.explain: The passage says 'traders were selling yams, plantains, tomatoes, and fish'.
procedure: Answer: Yams, plantains, tomatoes, and fish

questions.q:
Passage: 'Kojo was afraid of the dark. One night, the power went out. His mother gave him a torch. He held it tight and felt brave. From that day, he was no longer afraid.'

What was Kojo afraid of?
questions.explain: The passage says 'Kojo was afraid of the dark'.
procedure: Look for what he was afraid of

questions.q:
Passage: 'Kojo was afraid of the dark. One night, the power went out. His mother gave him a torch. He held it tight and felt brave. From that day, he was no longer afraid.'

What did his mother give him?
questions.explain: The passage says 'his mother gave him a torch'.
procedure: Look for what she gave him

questions.q:
Passage: 'The football match was exciting. In the last minute, Kwame scored the winning goal. The crowd cheered loudly. His team won the cup.'

Who scored the winning goal?
options: A player from the other team
questions.explain: The passage says 'Kwame scored the winning goal'.

questions.q:
Passage: 'The football match was exciting. In the last minute, Kwame scored the winning goal. The crowd cheered loudly. His team won the cup.'

When did Kwame score?
questions.explain: The passage says 'in the last minute, Kwame scored'.

questions.q:
Passage: 'Nana has a small garden behind her house. She grows tomatoes, pepper, and okra. Every evening, she waters the plants. She sells the vegetables at the market.'

What does Nana grow?
questions.explain: The passage lists what she grows.

questions.q:
Passage: 'Nana has a small garden behind her house. She grows tomatoes, pepper, and okra. Every evening, she waters the plants. She sells the vegetables at the market.'

When does she water the plants?
questions.explain: The passage says 'every evening, she waters the plants'.

questions.q:
Passage: 'The library is a quiet place. Students come to read and study. The librarian helps them find books. Everyone must be silent in the library.'

What is the main rule in the library?
questions.explain: The passage says 'everyone must be silent in the library'.
procedure: 'Everyone must be silent in the library'

questions.q:
Passage: 'The library is a quiet place. Students come to read and study. The librarian helps them find books. Everyone must be silent in the library.'

Who helps students find books?
questions.explain: The passage says 'the librarian helps them find books'.

questions.q:
Passage: 'The library is a quiet place. Students come to read and study. The librarian helps them find books. Everyone must be silent in the library.'

What is the main idea of this passage?
options: Librarians earn a lot of money
The library is a place for quiet reading and study
questions.answer: The library is a place for quiet reading and study
questions.explain: The whole passage is about what the library is for — reading, studying, and being quiet.
procedure: Think about what the whole passage is about
It describes the library, what people do there, and the rules
The main idea is: it's a place for quiet reading and study
Answer: The library is a place for quiet reading and study

procedure: 'As well' is a phrase, not one word

questions.q: What is an idiom?
options: A phrase whose meaning is different from its literal words
questions.answer: A phrase whose meaning is different from its literal words
questions.explain: An idiom is a phrase whose actual meaning is different from the literal words.
procedure: Their meaning is NOT the literal meaning
Example: 'It's raining cats and dogs' = raining heavily
Answer: A phrase whose meaning is different from its literal words

questions.q: What does 'It's raining cats and dogs' mean?
options: Cats and dogs are falling from the sky
questions.explain: 'Raining cats and dogs' is an idiom for very heavy rain.
procedure: The literal meaning is impossible (cats and dogs don't fall from the sky)
Actual meaning: it's raining very heavily

questions.q: What does 'a piece of cake' mean?
questions.explain: 'A piece of cake' means something is very easy.
procedure: Example: 'The test was a piece of cake' = the test was very easy
Answer: Something very easy to do

questions.q: What does 'break a leg' mean?
questions.explain: 'Break a leg' is a way to wish someone good luck — especially before a performance.
procedure: It does NOT mean break a bone

questions.q: What does 'let the cat out of the bag' mean?
questions.explain: 'Let the cat out of the bag' means to reveal a secret.
procedure: Literal meaning: freeing a cat from a bag

questions.q: What does 'under the weather' mean?
questions.explain: 'Under the weather' means feeling unwell or sick.
procedure: Actual meaning: feeling sick or unwell
Example: 'I'm feeling under the weather' = I'm feeling sick

questions.q: What is a proverb?
options: A short saying that gives advice or a truth
questions.answer: A short saying that gives advice or a truth
questions.explain: A proverb is a short wise saying that gives advice or expresses a truth.
procedure: Answer: A short saying that gives advice or a truth

questions.q: What does the proverb 'Actions speak louder than words' mean?
options: What people do matters more than what they say
Words are more important than actions
questions.answer: What people do matters more than what they say
questions.explain: 'Actions speak louder than words' means what you DO matters more than what you SAY.
procedure: It says actions are MORE important
Actual meaning: what people do matters more than what they say
Answer: What people do matters more than what they say

questions.q: What does the proverb 'A stitch in time saves nine' mean?
options: Fixing problems early prevents bigger problems later
questions.answer: Fixing problems early prevents bigger problems later
questions.explain: This proverb means dealing with a problem early saves effort later.
procedure: Literal: sewing one stitch now saves nine stitches later
Actual meaning: fix small problems early
Answer: Fixing problems early prevents bigger problems later

questions.q: What does the proverb 'Practice makes perfect' mean?
options: Practising a lot leads to improvement
questions.answer: Practising a lot leads to improvement
questions.explain: This proverb means the more you practise, the better you get.
procedure: Actual meaning: the more you practise, the better you become
Answer: Practising a lot leads to improvement

questions.q: What does the proverb 'Birds of a feather flock together' mean?
options: People with similar interests tend to spend time together
questions.answer: People with similar interests tend to spend time together
questions.explain: This proverb means people who are similar tend to be friends.
procedure: Literal: birds with the same feathers stay together
Actual meaning: people who are similar tend to be friends
Answer: People with similar interests tend to spend time together

questions.q: What does the proverb 'Don't judge a book by its cover' mean?
options: Don't judge people by their appearance
questions.answer: Don't judge people by their appearance
questions.explain: This proverb means don't judge people by how they look — look at who they really are.
procedure: Literal: don't judge a book by its cover
Actual meaning: don't judge people by their appearance
Answer: Don't judge people by their appearance

questions.q: What does 'Once bitten, twice shy' mean?
options: You become more careful after a bad experience
questions.answer: You become more careful after a bad experience
questions.explain: This proverb means after being hurt once, you become more careful.
procedure: Actual meaning: after a bad experience, you become more careful
Answer: You become more careful after a bad experience

questions.q: What does 'Better late than never' mean?
options: It's better to do something late than not at all
questions.answer: It's better to do something late than not at all
questions.explain: This proverb means it's better to do something — even late — than never do it.
procedure: Actual meaning: doing something late is better than never doing it
Answer: It's better to do something late than not at all

questions.q: What does 'The early bird catches the worm' mean?
questions.explain: This proverb means people who act early have an advantage.
procedure: Literal: the bird that wakes up early gets the worm
Actual meaning: people who start early succeed
Answer: People who start early succeed

questions.q: What does 'All that glitters is not gold' mean?
options: Not everything that looks good is actually good
questions.answer: Not everything that looks good is actually good
questions.explain: This proverb means not everything that looks valuable or attractive is truly valuable.
procedure: Literal: shiny things are not always gold
Actual meaning: not everything that looks good is actually good
Answer: Not everything that looks good is actually good

questions.q: What does 'Many hands make light work' mean?
options: When people work together, the work is easier
questions.answer: When people work together, the work is easier
questions.explain: This proverb means teamwork makes difficult tasks easier.
procedure: Literal: many hands (people) make work light (easy)
Actual meaning: teamwork makes difficult tasks easier
Answer: When people work together, the work is easier

questions.q: What does 'A friend in need is a friend indeed' mean?
options: A true friend helps you when you need it most
questions.answer: A true friend helps you when you need it most
questions.explain: This proverb means you know who your true friends are when you're in trouble.
procedure: Literal: a friend in need (when you need) is a friend indeed (truly a friend)
Actual meaning: a true friend helps you when you need it most
Answer: A true friend helps you when you need it most

questions.q: What does 'Look before you leap' mean?
questions.explain: This proverb means think before you act — don't rush into things.
procedure: Actual meaning: think carefully before acting

questions.q: What does 'Where there's a will, there's a way' mean?
options: If you really want something, you'll find a way to achieve it
questions.answer: If you really want something, you'll find a way to achieve it
questions.explain: This proverb means determination leads to solutions.
procedure: Actual meaning: if you really want something, you'll find a way
Answer: If you really want something, you'll find a way to achieve it

questions.q: What is a paragraph?
options: A group of sentences about one topic
questions.answer: A group of sentences about one topic
questions.explain: A paragraph is a group of sentences that focus on one idea or topic.
procedure: A paragraph is more than one sentence
All sentences in a paragraph relate to the same topic
Usually has a topic sentence + supporting sentences
Answer: A group of sentences about one topic

questions.q: What is a topic sentence?
options: The longest sentence in a paragraph
The sentence that tells the main idea of a paragraph
The last sentence in a paragraph
questions.answer: The sentence that tells the main idea of a paragraph
questions.explain: A topic sentence states the main idea of a paragraph.
procedure: The topic sentence tells what the paragraph is about
Answer: The sentence that tells the main idea of a paragraph

questions.q: What should every composition have?
questions.explain: A good composition has a clear beginning (introduction), middle (body), and end (conclusion).
procedure: Middle: develops the idea with details
Answer: A beginning, middle, and end

questions.q: What is an introduction?
options: The beginning — it introduces the topic
questions.answer: The beginning — it introduces the topic
questions.explain: An introduction is the opening of a composition that sets the topic.
procedure: The introduction is the start of a composition
It tells the reader what the composition is about
It should be interesting enough to make the reader want to continue
Answer: The beginning — it introduces the topic

questions.q: What is a conclusion?
options: The ending — it wraps up the composition
questions.answer: The ending — it wraps up the composition
questions.explain: A conclusion is the ending of a composition that summarises the main points.
procedure: It gives the reader a final thought
Answer: The ending — it wraps up the composition

questions.q: What is an informal letter?
options: A letter to a friend or family member
A letter to a school principal
questions.answer: A letter to a friend or family member
questions.explain: An informal letter is casual — written to friends or family.
procedure: Structure is less strict than formal letters
Answer: A letter to a friend or family member

questions.q: What is a formal letter?
options: A letter to a company, official, or organisation
questions.answer: A letter to a company, official, or organisation
questions.explain: A formal letter is official — written to someone in a professional context.
procedure: Answer: A letter to a company, official, or organisation

questions.q: How should an informal letter end?
questions.explain: Informal letters end with casual phrases like 'Best wishes' or 'Yours friend'.
procedure: 'Yours faithfully' and 'Yours sincerely' are for formal letters

questions.q: How should a formal letter end?
questions.explain: Formal letters end with 'Yours faithfully' or 'Yours sincerely'.
procedure: Use 'Yours faithfully' if you don't know the person's name
Use 'Yours sincerely' if you know the name

questions.q: What is a narrative composition?
options: A story — describing events that happened
questions.answer: A story — describing events that happened
questions.explain: A narrative composition tells a story with characters and events.
procedure: It has characters, events, and usually a plot
Example: 'A Day I Will Never Forget'
Answer: A story — describing events that happened

questions.q: What is a descriptive composition?
options: A composition that describes something in detail
questions.answer: A composition that describes something in detail
questions.explain: A descriptive composition paints a picture with words.
procedure: It describes a person, place, or thing
Uses sensory details (sight, sound, smell, taste, touch)
Answer: A composition that describes something in detail

questions.q: What is an argumentative composition?
options: A composition that argues for or against an opinion
questions.answer: A composition that argues for or against an opinion
questions.explain: An argumentative composition presents a view and supports it with reasons.
procedure: It takes a position (for or against)
Answer: A composition that argues for or against an opinion

questions.q: What does a good composition have at the start?
options: An interesting opening that hooks the reader
questions.answer: An interesting opening that hooks the reader
questions.explain: A good composition starts with an interesting opening that grabs attention.
procedure: The opening is the first impression
It should make the reader want to continue
Options: a question, an interesting fact, a quote, a description
Answer: An interesting opening that hooks the reader

questions.q: How many paragraphs should a short composition have?
questions.explain: A short composition should have at least three paragraphs — introduction, body, and conclusion.
procedure: Each paragraph should have one main idea

questions.q: What should you do before writing a composition?
options: Ask a friend to write it
questions.explain: Planning helps you organise your thoughts before writing.
procedure: List what you'll cover in each paragraph
This makes writing clearer and easier

questions.q: What is a title?
questions.explain: A title is the name of a composition — it tells the reader what the piece is about.
procedure: The title is at the top
It's the name of the composition
Answer: The name of a composition

questions.q: What should every sentence in a composition begin with?
questions.explain: Every sentence must start with a capital letter.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a dialogue in a composition?
options: To show characters speaking to each other
questions.answer: To show characters speaking to each other
questions.explain: Dialogue is when characters speak — it's shown with quotation marks.
procedure: Shown with quotation marks: "Hello," she said.
It makes stories more alive and interesting
Answer: To show characters speaking to each other

questions.q: Which is the correct way to write dialogue?
questions.explain: Dialogue needs quotation marks around the spoken words.
procedure: Spoken words go in quotation marks
The comma goes inside the quotation marks

questions.q: Why should we read our composition after writing it?
questions.explain: Reading over your work helps you catch spelling, grammar, and punctuation mistakes.
procedure: After writing, read it out loud or silently
Look for errors in spelling, grammar, punctuation
Answer: To find and fix mistakes
